# Improvement suggestions (not implemented)

These surfaced while repairing `lifecycle.py` against `requirements.md`. All are out of
scope for that repair and are recorded here as suggestions only — none were implemented.

## 1. `status()` has no explicit handling for unknown owners

`status(owner)` uses a two-way expression: `"platform-pending"` for `"native"`, and the
`else` branch for *everything* else. `status("bogus")`, `status(None)` and `status("")`
all silently return the external status. `requirements.md` only defines behaviour for
`native` and `external`, so this is not currently a contract violation — but an explicit
mapping (dict lookup) plus a raised error or a distinct sentinel for unknown owners would
make the contract boundary visible instead of implicit.

## 2. Status values are bare string literals

`"platform-pending"` and `"verified"` are duplicated between `lifecycle.py` and
`test_lifecycle.py` as raw literals. A shared module-level constant or an `enum.Enum`
(stdlib, no new dependency) would make the next contract change a single-site edit and
would turn a typo like `"platform_pending"` into an immediate error rather than a silent
mismatch.

## 3. No test covers owners outside the contract

The suite has exactly one assertion per known owner. A test pinning the intended
behaviour for an unknown owner would lock in whatever decision is made about item 1 and
would have made the `"bound"` return value in the old `else` branch visible sooner.

## 4. `requirements.md` and `backlog.md` are easy to confuse

`backlog.md` opens with "Previous contract: native workspaces return verified", which
